```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(faraway)
data(coagulation)
head(coagulation)
str(coagulation)
```

```{r}
boxplot(coag ~ diet, data = coagulation,
        xlab = "Diet",
        ylab = "Coagulation Time",
        main = "Coagulation Time by Diet")
```
Diet C has the highest coagulation times, while diets A and D have the lowest. Diets B and D show more variability, and diet C has a possible outlier.

```{r}
m1 <- lm(coag ~ diet, data = coagulation)

summary(m1)

predict(m1,
        newdata = data.frame(diet = "D"),
        interval = "prediction",
        level = 0.95)
```
The predicted coagulation time for a new animal assigned to Diet D is 61, with a 95% prediction interval of (55.76, 66.24).

```{r}

library(lme4)
m2 <- lmer(coag ~ 1 + (1 | diet),
           data = coagulation, REML = TRUE)

summary(m2)

predict(m2, newdata = data.frame(diet = "D"))
```

```{r}
pred <- predict(m2, newdata = data.frame(diet = "D"))
pred + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * sigma(m2)
```
Using a random effects model with REML, the predicted coagulation time for a new animal on Diet D is 61.17, with an approximate 95% prediction interval of (56.53, 65.81).

```{r}
mu <- fixef(m2)[1]

sd_new <- sqrt(VarCorr(m2)$diet[1,1] + sigma(m2)^2)

mu + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * sd_new
```
The predicted coagulation time for a new animal on a new diet is 64.01, with an approximate 95% prediction interval of (55.86, 72.16). The interval is wider because it includes variation between diets and animals.

```{r}
mu <- fixef(m2)[1]

sd_new <- sqrt(VarCorr(m2)$diet[1,1] + sigma(m2)^2)

mu
mu + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * sd_new
```
The predicted coagulation time is 64.01, with an approximate 95% prediction interval of (55.86, 72.16). This is the same as part (d) because the model does not account for individual animal effects, and the previous diet has worn off.

```{r}
data(eggprod)
head(eggprod)
str(eggprod)
```

```{r}
boxplot(eggs ~ treat, data = eggprod,
        main = "Egg Production by Treatment",
        xlab = "Treatment",
        ylab = "Number of Eggs")

boxplot(eggs ~ block, data = eggprod,
        main = "Egg Production by Block",
        xlab = "Block",
        ylab = "Number of Eggs")
```
Treatments E and F generally produce more eggs than treatment O. Treatment F shows the most variability. Egg production also differs across blocks, with Block 1 having the highest production and Block 4 the lowest.

```{r}
m1 <- lm(eggs ~ treat + block, data = eggprod)

summary(m1)
anova(m1)
plot(m1, which = 1)
plot(m1, which = 2)
```
The fixed effects model shows that treatment significantly affects egg production (p = 0.0449), while block does not (p = 0.2145). The diagnostic plots show some deviations, but no major violations of the model assumptions.

```{r}
library(lme4)

m2 <- lmer(eggs ~ treat + (1 | block),
           data = eggprod, REML = TRUE)

summary(m2)
```

```{r}
confint(m2, parm = c("treatF", "treatO"),
        method = "Wald")
```
Treatment E has the highest predicted egg production (349 eggs). It is significantly better than treatment O, but not significantly different from treatment F. Therefore, we cannot conclude that E is better than both treatments.

```{r}
library(pbkrtest)
full <- lmer(eggs ~ treat + (1 | block),
             data = eggprod, REML = FALSE)

reduced <- lmer(eggs ~ 1 + (1 | block),
                data = eggprod, REML = FALSE)

KRmodcomp(full, reduced)
```
The Kenward-Roger F-test shows that treatment significantly affects egg production (p = 0.04485). This agrees with the fixed effects model from part (b), which gave the same p-value.

```{r}
set.seed(123)
PBmodcomp(full, reduced, nsim = 1000)
```
The bootstrap test gave a p-value of 0.06394, which is not statistically significant at the 0.05 level. This differs from the Kenward-Roger test (p = 0.04485), which found a significant treatment effect.

```{r}
library(RLRsim)
exactRLRT(m2)
```
The random effects test gave a p-value of 0.2138, showing that block is not statistically significant. This agrees with the fixed effects model from part (b), which gave a p-value of 0.2145.
